title: BCCI Postpones October 15 IPL Stakeholder Meeting as Modi Felicitates Asian Games Teams
excerpt: Franchise owners, broadcasters and 13 host associations were due in Mumbai; the board's officials are needed in Delhi instead, and no new date has been set.
body:
• The BCCI has postponed its October 15 IPL joint review meeting in Mumbai, with no new date announced, Cricbuzz reported.
  • The meeting clashed with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's felicitation in New Delhi of India's men's and women's teams and other medallists from the 20th Asian Games.
  • Franchise owners and CEOs, broadcasters and 13 host state associations were due at the Taj Santacruz at 6 p.m. on Thursday.
  • India's players will reroute via Delhi after Wednesday's fourth T20I before the final match against West Indies in Bengaluru on October 17.

The Board of Control for Cricket in India has postponed the IPL's joint review meeting scheduled for October 15 in Mumbai, after Prime Minister Narendra Modi's felicitation of India's Asian Games teams on the same day pulled the board's top officials to New Delhi. Stakeholders were informed on Tuesday, and no new date has been communicated, according to Cricbuzz.

Who was coming, and for what

The meeting was to bring IPL franchise owners and their chief executives together with broadcasters and the 13 state associations that host matches, at the Taj Santacruz at 6 p.m. on Thursday. It was billed as a joint review of the league ahead of its 20th season next year — the kind of session where scheduling, commercial and hosting questions for the coming cycle get worked through with everyone in one room.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=7NsVveqehKc

Why it moved

BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia's mail to stakeholders said the Prime Minister is scheduled to felicitate the Indian men's and women's teams for their performances at the recently concluded 20th Asian Games on October 15 in New Delhi, and that BCCI officials will be required to attend. Saikia added that requests for a postponement had also come from various stakeholders, and that the decision was taken to facilitate maximum participation in person. The revised date and venue will be communicated in due course, he wrote, regretting the inconvenience.

"Accordingly, BCCI officials will be required to attend the felicitation ceremony."

— Devajit Saikia, BCCI secretary, in his mail to stakeholders

What the review was meant to settle

Reporting on the postponement said the session's agenda was to work through issues from previous seasons and chalk out plans for IPL 2027, the league's 20th edition. That makes the gathering more than ceremonial: franchise owners, chief executives, broadcasters and the 13 hosting associations rarely sit in one room, and questions that need all of them — scheduling windows, hosting arrangements and the commercial calendar — tend to wait for exactly this kind of conclave. Postponing it indefinitely, rather than by a week, leaves those questions open while teams are already planning for next season.

A detour for the team

The felicitation also reshapes the national team's week. With the New Delhi function added to their itinerary, India's players will travel to the capital on Thursday instead of flying directly from Hyderabad to Bengaluru after the fourth T20I on Wednesday, October 14. They then proceed to Bengaluru for the fifth and final T20I against West Indies on October 17.

What to watch

For franchises and broadcasters, the substance has not changed — only the date is missing. The rescheduled session will still be the first full gathering to plan the league's 20th season, and its timing will signal how much of the calendar is already locked.
